This memorandum addresses the enforceability of the limitation of liability clause (Section 8.3) in the technology services agreement between Client and AlphaTech Inc. Based on analysis of relevant case law, statutory framework, and the specific contract terms, the clause is likely enforceable as written under Delaware law, which governs the agreement. Key precedents such as Hadley v. Baxendale support the exclusion of consequential damages when they are not foreseeable, and Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6) provides a procedural avenue to challenge claims that fall outside the liability cap. However, the clause exposes the Client to significant risk, particularly regarding uncapped liability for Vendor negligence (Section 8.1) and an overbroad non-compete (Section 12.1). We recommend pursuing a negotiated amendment to mutualize indemnification, narrow the non-compete, and carve out liability for data breaches and IP infringement. A motion to dismiss any claim exceeding the liability cap has been filed and served, which may resolve this issue procedurally.
